steps.page: How the app's other warnings look and behave
steps.intro: Real pictures from the app. Most already belong to one chat and leave once the problem is fixed.

steps.path: Every warning a chat can show
steps.headline: Every kind of warning in a chat today

calls.why: A card in the chat. Only in that chat. Stays until you answer or dismiss it. This is what the notice is pointing you to.
Inside the chat, under the last reply, with a red outline. Only in that chat. Goes away by itself the moment Claude replies again.

calls.call: An error from the AI service
calls.why: Inside the chat, with a red outline and Details. Only in that chat. Stays until your next message. Buttons to try again or switch model.
Inside the chat, a small red-outlined line with Try again. Only in that chat. Goes away once the connection works.
Inside the chat, in place of the reply. After you sign in it turns green, then goes away with your next message.

calls.call: A message that may not have arrived
calls.why: A row just above the message box. Only in that chat. Goes away once the message is confirmed, or when you press Dismiss.

calls.call: Starting up, or tools that failed
calls.why: A strip just above the message box. Only in that chat. Grey while it works, red if it fails. Goes away once the chat is ready.
A strip just above the message box on a phone. Only in that chat. Goes away once it reconnects, and keeps your draft.

calls.call: Something left out when the chat started
calls.why: An amber strip across the top of the chat. Only in that chat. It stays, because it is information rather than a problem to fix.
One floating spot for the whole app, used by about 40 messages like this one. Meant to leave after a few seconds. All share the stuck-timer bug.

steps.intro: Where the notice goes, when it shows, and what happens to your held-back message.

steps.path: The notice above the message box
steps.headline: Where should the notice sit?
steps.today: It floats over the bottom of the chat, in every chat, and stays until Claude goes quiet.
steps.checked: Read in the app's code on 2026-11-21, and matches your screenshot.
steps.problem: It covers your messages and follows you to chats it has nothing to do with.
steps.proposal: Three drawings of the same moment: a question is waiting, and you pressed Send. All three stay in their own chat and leave once you answer or send.

options.label: Strip above the box
options.caption: Same strip as "Connecting tools…" and the phone's "Reconnecting…".
pros: Works like the other warnings above the box, so nothing new to learn.
Sits right where your held-back message is.
cons: Pushes the chat up by one line while it shows.

from: The "Connecting tools…" strip above the message box
new: The words, and the two buttons inside the strip

options.label: Floating, per chat
options.caption: Today's look, but only in its own chat, and staying until you answer.
pros: Looks the same as today; only when it leaves changes.
cons: Still covers part of the chat while it stays, which is what bothers you now.
Any other floating notice would replace it.

options.label: In the chat
options.caption: A line right under the waiting question, like "No internet".
pros: Sits right beside the thing you need to answer.
cons: Scrolls away with the chat, so you can miss it.
When the thing waiting is a pop-up only on the terminal screen, there is no question in the chat to sit under.

steps.path: The notice above the message box
steps.headline: When should the notice appear?
steps.today: Only when you press Send and the message is held back.
steps.checked: Read in the app's code on 2026-11-21.
steps.problem: Claude's question is usually already on screen, so a notice before you send would repeat it.

options.label: After you press Send
options.summary: It only appears when your message is held back, as now.
pros: Never repeats a question you can already see.
Shows exactly when you need to know why nothing sent.
cons: You only learn something is waiting once you try to send.

options.label: Whenever something waits
options.summary: It shows as soon as Claude Code waits on you, even before you type.
pros: You know before you start typing.
cons: Shows on top of a question you can already see, most of the time.

steps.headline: Once you answer, should your held-back message send itself?
steps.today: Your message stays in the box. After answering, you press Send again yourself.
steps.checked: Read in the app's code on 2026-11-21.
steps.problem: Pressing Send twice is a small annoyance; a message sending itself later can be a surprise.

options.label: You press Send again
options.summary: The message waits in the box until you send it.
pros: Nothing sends without you pressing the button.
You can change or delete it first.

options.label: It sends itself
options.summary: The notice says your message will send once you answer, and it goes out as soon as you do.
cons: A message typed minutes ago could go out after you changed your mind.
A bigger change to how sending works, so more that could go wrong.

steps.path: The floating notices above the message box
steps.headline: Should I also fix the stuck timer for the other floating notices now?
steps.today: About 40 short notices, like "Not connected" or "Couldn't switch model", share the same stuck-timer bug.
steps.checked: Found by reading the shared notice code on 2026-11-21; the bug is in the one piece all of them use.
steps.problem: Any of them can stay on screen while Claude works, the same way this one did.
steps.proposal: Fix that one shared piece now. Yes: those notices leave on time, and that is the only change you would notice. No: they stay as they are.
